17-13-0303-C (1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans - Zoning Map Amendment
3040-3042 North Lincoln Avenue, Chicago, Illinois 60657

Proposed Zoning: B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: 6,250 square feet

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is seeking a Type I Zoning Map Amendment, with secondary
relief for an Administrative Adjustment and a Variation, pursuant to Section
17-13-0300 of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, in order to permit the
redevelopment of the subject property with a new four-story mixed-use
building. The programming for the proposed new building calls for the
establishment of a single commercial unit at the front of the ground floor,
comprising the street facing frontage, and a total of nine (9) dwelling units
to be distributed on and between the 2™ through 4" floors. Interior off-street
parking for eight (8) vehicles will be situated within the rear of the ground
floor, with access from the public alley. The proposed improvements will
be masonry in construction and wil] measure approximately 43 feet-0 inches
in height (4 floor ceiling).

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 18,622 square feet (2.98 FAR) (Total Building)
1,308 square feet (Ground Floor Commercial Space)

(B) The Project’s Density (Lot Area Per Dwelling Unit): 9 units (694 square feet)
(C) The amount of off-street parking: *8 automobile spaces; 10 bicycle spaces

*The subject property is located on a designated Pedestrian Retail Street, within 2,640
linear feet of the entrance to the Southport Brown Line (CTA) Train Station, thereby
qualifying as a Transit Served Location (TSL), under the current Chicago Zoning
Ordinance [17-10-0102-B] and triggering a distinct Parking Standard [17-3-0308] for
dwelling units, which limits the maximum allowable off-street residential parking ratio
to 50%. The programming for the subject development calls for the construction of a
new mixed-use building that will feature nine (9) dwelling units, seven of which will be
three-bedroom units intended for family occupancy and two of which will be two-
bedroom units intended for work-from-home occupancy by singles or couples.
Applying the TSL Parking Standard results in a maximum by-right allowance of 5 off-
street parking spaces, which was deemed insufficient by community stakeholders.
Therefore, in consideration of current market demand for larger format rental housing
units with designated off-street parking, as was repeated by local liaisons, the
Applicant is proposing to increase the number of off-street automobile parking spaces
to serve this transit-oriented development, so that all but one of the dwelling units will

have dedicated onsite parking. As such, the Applicant is seeking an Administrative
Adjustment - in conjunction with this Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment, to increase the
maximum automobile parking ratio for a transit served location (TSL) — from 5 spaces
(56%) to 8 spaces (89%). [Section 17-3-0308-B; Section 17-13-1003-EE.]

(D) — Setbacks: a. Front Setback: 0 foot-0 inches
b. *Rear Setback: 0 feet-0 inches

c. Side Setbacks:
West: 0 feet-0 inches
East: 0 feet-0 inches

*In order to accommodate the provision of larger format dwelling units intended for occupancy
by growing families that desire the flexibility and financial viability of renting, which were current
market observations specifically echoed during many months of ongoing community engagement,
the Applicant had to amplify the residential floorplates for the upper floors, allowing for longer
layouts, as well as inset balconies for each unit. Such building orientation and scale is completely
compatible with the pattern of improvements on this mixed-use block of Lincoln Avenue, where
almost all of the properties are occupied by buildings that span the entire width and depth of their
respective site, including both of the immediately adjacent developments, as well as the existing
commercial building that the Applicant will be replacing if this Type 1 Zoning Amendment is
approved and ratified. As such, the Applicant is seeking this Variation, to reduce the minimum
rear setback for floors containing dwelling units from 30 feet to zero. [Section 17-3-0405-A].

(E) Building Height: 43 feet-0 inches (underside of 4" Floor ceiling beam)

COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 17-3-0308
Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations

In all B and C districts, any new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail
station entrance must satisfy all of the following specific criteria:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B.

The project calls for the construction and occupancy of a new four-story mixed-use
development at the subject property, which qualifies as a Transit-Served Location (TSL) due to its
proximity to the Southport CTA Brown Line Train Station. The ground floor of the new proposed
development will feature a single commercial / retail unit, occupying and activating the entire
Pedestrian Retail Street frontage along Lincoln Avenue. Nine (9) dwelling units will be distributed
on and between the 2” floor through the 4" floor, seven of which will feature three bedrooms and
two of which will feature two bedrooms, intended to accommodate growing families and work-
from-home singles and couples. The front units on the 2™ floor and 3" floor will each feature a
private recessed balcony, while the residents of the 4" floor units will have direct access to a
communal roof deck overlooking the bustling mixed-use corridor. The design and functionality of
the dwelling units were developed in a conscious effort to attract and provide under-resourced
economical rental housing for families and/or work-from-home dwellers, so to ensure ongoing
activation of the property from ground up and to add more vested members to the immediate
community, who will patronize and help to revitalize the existing businesses, while the inclusion
of the newly rendered commercial / retail space is intended to encourage interest from a local
business and/or service provider seeking to support the residents and occupants of the
neighborhood. Rounding out the development is enclosed parking for eight (8) vehicles, each space
adapted with an electric (EVSE) charging station, by request and recommendation of the local
Alderman and community liaisons, in an effort to further reduce the carbon footprint of the new
development, while allowing residents the security of having one personal vehicle, actively
mitigating private consumption of the limited public parking facilities in the neighborhood and
further advancing the City’s land use and planning policies. In addition hereto, and in furtherance
of these sustainable policies and goals, the new development also accommodates enclosed parking
and storage for at least ten (10) bicycles, e-bicycles, scooters and/or strollers. Such proposed
parking provisions represents a 89% automobile-to-unit ratio and a 110% bicycle-to-unit ratio, so
that the residents of all but one of the units will be designated their own off-street vehicular parking
space, thereby mitigating the demand on scarce public parking resources in the neighborhood and
easing parking congestion in the streets, while still promoting reliance on the many other
meaningful multi-modal forms of nearby public transit and environmentally conscious
transportation.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504, (except
paragraph H if the project is not located along a pedestrian street), pertaining to
pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail streets, even if the project is not located along
a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street.
